denial.premise_measurement: Baseline at commit 71de6e8e7, `probe.py game/ui/select setup_sel_menu --ops`: real 82, insns T123/O123, multiset 2t, fresh fuzzy 92.0244%, RELOC-SYMBOL SCREEN clean. (a) Deleting the `u8* entries = bss + 1824;` local and writing `entry = (VmuMenuEntry*)(bss + off + 1824)` REGRESSED: real 123 at T123/O124, multiset 3t, and it LOST count parity -- MWCC reassociated to `addi(off,1824); add(base)` exactly as claim.law.two-use-preoffset-pointer-keeps-add-then-addi.20260831.v1 predicts for a single-use intermediate, adding an `addi` and still emitting `lwz r0,0(r4)`. (b) THE UPDATE-LOAD FORM WORKS: rewriting the guard as `entry = (VmuMenuEntry*)(bss + off); if ((entry = (VmuMenuEntry*)((u8*)entry + 1824))->text == NULL)` produced the target's `@0x144 lwzu r0,1824(r4)` off `@0x140 add r4,r31,r5`, REGAINED count parity T123/O123, and took the opcode multiset to IDENTICAL (123/123) with regnorm genuine structural rows down to ONE. But it is not a keep: real ROSE 82 -> 100 and fresh objdiff fuzzy fell 92.0244% -> 91.9837%, so both arbiters are flat-to-worse and only the multiset improved -- and the multiset gain does not buy postprocessor eligibility either, because probe.py reports `IDENTICAL (123/123) -- but 2 IMMEDIATE word(s) differ at aligned same-opcode positions: NOT pure reorder, NOT schedule-class`. (c) Extending the walking cursor to the y write, on top of (b), was clearly negative: fresh fuzzy 91.9837% -> 91.1545%, real 102. All three reverted with `probe.py game/ui/select setup_sel_menu --discard`.

hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: One probe that converts ONLY the case-8/13 x/y pair to a cursor walk, leaving case 5/10 alone. If the `@0x18c` IMMEDIATE row closes while the `@0x100` one does not, the two sites are independent and the `one lever` framing is wrong -- and probe (c) has already shown a single-field extension is negative in the other arm, so a negative here would close the cursor axis outright.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes -- `fnasm game/ui/select setup_sel_menu 0xe8:0x150 --diff` and `0x180:0x198 --diff` at the baseline show the target's `@0x118 addi r7,r4,828` cursor and both `stw r0,0(r7)` stores against our `stw r0,728(r4)` / `stw r0,724(r5)`. The combined-arm probe itself is NOT run.
hypothesis.statement: The two IMMEDIATE rows and the five ordering clusters are ONE lever, and the update-load should be re-probed only after it. The target stores through a WALKING POINTER at displacement 0 (`@0x100 stw r0,0(r7)` and `@0x18c stw r0,0(r7)`) where we store at `stw r0,728(r4)` and `stw r0,724(r5)` -- 728 and 724 are 712+offsetof(y) and 712+offsetof(x), i.e. the two ends of the `field +=` cursor this function ALREADY uses at `*(s32*)(field += 712 + offsetof(OptMenuLayout, x)) -= baseChoice;`. Probe (c) shows the cursor cannot simply be extended one field at a time; the next lane should instead reconstruct the WHOLE case-5/10 and case-8/13 arms as one continuous cursor walk in target order, then re-add the update-load, and arbitrate the combined state rather than each step.
